title: Knowledge check: Watching Reactive State

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Watching Reactive State”?
options: Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
Use computed() for every side effect.
Leave stale asynchronous work running and let it overwrite newer results.
Expect watch() to run immediately by default for every source.
questions.answer_key: Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Watching Reactive State directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “The watch() API”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use computed() for every side effect.
Leave stale asynchronous work running and let it overwrite newer results.
Expect watch() to run immediately by default for every source.
Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
questions.answer_key: Use watch() for explicit sources or watchEffect() for automatically tracked dependencies when a side effect is required; clean up asynchronous work.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “The watch() API”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Watching Reactive State” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
